# Toast

Transient status messages at the bottom of the screen. Toasts stack with a compressed fan when several are queued, hover to expand, follow a promise from loading to its result, and update in place.

```tsx
import { toast } from "@/components/ui/toast"

<Button onClick={() => toast("Your changes have been saved.")}>
  Show toast
</Button>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add toast
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/toast/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

Add `<Toaster />` once to your root layout: it renders the fixed viewport and is required for toasts to appear.

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { Toaster } from "@/components/ui/toast"

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        {children}
        <Toaster />
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { toast, useToast } from "@/components/ui/toast"

// Imperative: works anywhere (Server Action results, event handlers, outside React)
toast("File saved.")
toast.success("Uploaded.")
toast.error("Something went wrong.")
toast.warning("Disk space low.")
toast.info("Version 2.4 available.")

// Work in flight: one toast that follows the promise to its result
toast.promise(saveChanges(), {
  loading: "Saving…",
  success: "Saved.",
  error: "Couldn't save.",
})

// Beside the element that raised it, instead of the stack
toast.success("Link copied", { anchor: event.currentTarget })

// Close one toast by id, or all of them
toast.dismiss(id)
toast.dismiss()

// Hook: same API, inside React components
function MyComponent() {
  const { toast } = useToast()
  return <Button onClick={() => toast("Done!")}>Save</Button>
}
```

## Variants

Five semantic variants: `default`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, and `info`. Every toast is the same neutral elevated card (border + shadow); the status colour is carried by the icon, so the variants stay calm and never fight the page. The buttons fire the real thing.

```tsx
toast("Changes saved successfully.")
toast.success("File uploaded.", { description: "profile-photo.png is ready." })
toast.warning("Storage almost full.", { description: "You have 200 MB remaining." })
toast.error("Upload failed.", { description: "The server returned a 413 error." })
toast.info("New version available.", { description: "Refresh the page to get v2.4.0." })
```

## Loading

`toast.loading` shows a spinner and stays up until you raise the same `id` again with the result. The card is updated in place: the spinner cross-fades into the result icon and the title rolls to its new line, so it reads as one piece of work finishing rather than a second message arriving.

```tsx
const id = toast.loading("Uploading 3 files…", { description: "Keep this tab open." })
await upload(files)
toast.success("Upload complete.", { id, description: "3 files are ready." })
```

## Promise

`toast.promise` does the loading-then-result dance for you. Each message can be a title, a full options object, or a function of the resolved value (or the error). It hands the promise back, so `await toast.promise(save(), …)` still returns the value or throws.

```tsx
toast.promise(saveChanges(), {
  loading: "Saving changes…",
  success: (count) => `Saved ${count} changes.`,
  error: {
    title: "Couldn't save.",
    description: "You're offline. We'll retry when you reconnect.",
  },
})
```

## Update in place

Give a toast an `id` and raising it again never stacks a copy. The card moves to the front, its timer restarts, and it replays a short cue so the repeat still registers: a pop for a confirmation, a shake for an error or a warning. Press either button several times to see it.

```tsx
toast.success("Link copied.", { id: "copy-link" })
toast.error("Wrong code.", { id: "verify", description: "Check the code and try again." })
```

## Anchored

Pass an `anchor` and the toast becomes a small bubble beside the element that raised it: a “Copied” next to the copy button rather than a card at the far bottom of the screen. It sits above the element (below it when the element is near the top of the screen), stays up for 1.5 seconds, and closes as soon as the page scrolls or resizes, since it would otherwise drift away from what it describes. The bubble itself is hidden from assistive tech; an always-mounted live region announces it instead.

```tsx
<Button
  onClick={(event) =>
    toast.success("Link copied", { anchor: event.currentTarget })
  }
>
  Copy link
</Button>
```

## With action

Pass an `action` object with a `label` and `onClick` handler. The button appears below the description and is announced as an accessible action by screen readers.

```tsx
toast({
  title: "Email sent.",
  description: "Your message was delivered to alex@example.com.",
  action: {
    label: "Undo",
    onClick: () => toast("Send undone."),
  },
})
```

## Stacking

When multiple toasts are queued they compress into a fan: older toasts peek behind the newest one at decreasing scale and offset. Hover (or focus) the stack to expand all toasts to their full size with a 16px gap. Up to three toasts show in the collapsed fan; any beyond that are hidden until older ones are dismissed. On a touch screen, swipe a toast to the right to dismiss it: the card follows your finger.

```tsx
// Fire several toasts and hover the stack to expand
toast({ title: "Build passed", variant: "success" })
toast({ title: "Deploy queued", description: "Estimated time: 2 min." })
toast({ title: "Preview ready", variant: "info" })
```

## Persistent

Pass `duration: Infinity` to keep the toast until the user explicitly dismisses it. Useful for critical alerts. For work in progress, prefer `toast.loading`, which persists on its own and resolves in place.

```tsx
toast({
  title: "Syncing in background.",
  description: "This won't dismiss automatically.",
  duration: Infinity,
})
```

## API reference

### Toaster

Renders the fixed, bottom-centered Radix Toast viewport, the anchored bubbles and a polite live region. Mount it once in the root layout. Forwards the Radix `Toast.Viewport` props and native `<ol>` props to the viewport, and `className` merges last there (move it with `bottom-6`, say). The stack keeps ownership of the viewport height; your pointer and focus handlers run alongside its expand and collapse.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| swipeDirection | "right" \| "left" \| "up" \| "down" | "right" | Direction a toast is swiped to dismiss it. |
| swipeThreshold | number | 50 | Distance in pixels a swipe must travel to dismiss. |
| hotkey | string[] | ["F8"] | Keys that move focus to the toast stack. |
| label | string | "Notifications ({hotkey})" | Accessible name of the viewport region; `{hotkey}` is replaced with the keys. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-state | On each toast: `"open"` or `"closed"` (Radix). |
| data-swipe | On each toast while swiped: `"start"`, `"move"`, `"cancel"` or `"end"` (Radix). |
| data-side | On an anchored bubble: `"top"` or `"bottom"` of its element. |

| CSS variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| --radix-toast-swipe-move-x | Horizontal offset while a toast is being swiped; the card follows it. |
| --radix-toast-swipe-end-x | Horizontal offset where a swipe ended, for the dismiss exit. |

### toast()

Raises a toast from anywhere: `toast("Saved.")`, `toast("Saved.", options)` or `toast(options)`. Returns the toast's id.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | string | - | A stable id. Raising it again while on screen updates that toast in place and replays a pop or shake. |
| title | React.ReactNode | - | The headline. |
| description | React.ReactNode | - | Supporting text under the title. |
| variant | "default" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "info" \| "loading" | "default" | The status icon. `destructive` is announced assertively, `loading` shows a spinner and persists. |
| duration | number | 5000 | Auto-dismiss delay in ms: `1500` when anchored, `Infinity` for `loading`. Pass `Infinity` to persist. |
| action | { label: string; onClick: () => void } | - | A button below the description, a Radix `Action` with the label as its `altText`. |
| anchor | HTMLElement \| null | - | Shows a small icon-and-title bubble beside this element instead of the stack (no close button, no action). Closes on scroll or resize. |

### toast.success / warning / error / info / loading

Shortcuts: `(title, options?)` with the variant set (`error` sets `destructive`). Options are the `toast()` options without `title` and `variant`. Each returns the id.

### toast.promise

`toast.promise(promise, messages, options?)`: one toast that shows `loading`, then turns into the result in place. Returns the promise, so awaiting it still yields the value or throws.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| promise* | Promise<T> \| (() => Promise<T>) | - | The work to follow. |
| messages.loading* | React.ReactNode | - | The title while pending. |
| messages.success* | ReactNode \| ToastOptions \| ((value: T) => ReactNode \| ToastOptions) | - | Shown on resolve, as a `success` toast. |
| messages.error* | ReactNode \| ToastOptions \| ((error: unknown) => ReactNode \| ToastOptions) | - | Shown on reject, as a `destructive` toast. |

### toast.dismiss

`toast.dismiss(id?)`: closes one toast by id, or every open toast when called with no id.

### useToast

Returns `{ toast, dismiss }`, the same imperative API, for use inside components.

### useToastStore

Low-level: subscribes to the queue and returns the current `ToastData[]`, for a custom renderer.

### TOAST_DURATION / ANCHORED_TOAST_DURATION

The default auto-dismiss delays in ms: `5000` for a stacked toast, `1500` for an anchored one.

## FAQ

### Should I call toast(...) or use the useToast() hook?

Both share the same API. The imperative `toast(...)` works anywhere, including Server Action results, event handlers, and code outside React, while `useToast()` returns the same `toast` plus a `dismiss` function for use inside components. Reach for the hook only when you want the matching `dismiss` helper at hand.

### Why do my toasts never appear?

You almost certainly forgot to render `<Toaster />` once in your root layout. It draws the fixed viewport that every toast portals into, so without it the calls succeed silently but nothing shows.

### How do I stop the same message from stacking up?

Give it an `id`. Raising a toast whose id is still on screen updates that card in place, moves it to the front and restarts its timer, then replays a pop (confirmations) or a shake (errors and warnings) so the repeat is still noticed. Without an id every call is a new toast.

### When should I use toast.promise instead of loading plus success?

Whenever the work is a single promise. `toast.promise(work, { loading, success, error })` shows the spinner, then turns the same card into the result, and returns the promise so you can still await it. Use `toast.loading` with an id when the result arrives from somewhere else, such as a websocket event.

### Can a toast appear next to the button that raised it?

Yes: pass `anchor: event.currentTarget`. The toast becomes a small icon-and-title bubble beside that element for 1.5 seconds instead of a card in the bottom stack, and it closes on scroll or resize. It has no close button or action, so keep it to a word or two, such as "Copied".

### How do I make a toast persist until dismissed?

Pass `duration: Infinity` in the options object. The default is 5000 ms, and `loading` toasts persist on their own. The toast stays up until the user clicks its Close button or your code calls `toast.dismiss(id)` with the id returned from `toast(...)`.

### What is the difference between toast.error and a destructive variant?

They are the same thing. `toast.error(...)` is a shortcut that sets `variant: "destructive"`, which is the role name used across the design system for danger styling. It is also the one variant announced assertively, so a screen reader interrupts for it; the others wait their turn.

### How do I add an Undo button to a toast?

Pass an `action` object with a `label` and an `onClick`. It renders below the description as a Radix Toast Action with the label as its `altText`, so screen readers announce it as an actionable control.

### Why do queued toasts collapse into a fan?

Stacking is handled by the Toaster: older toasts compress behind the newest at decreasing scale and offset so the stack stays calm. Hover or focus the stack to expand all of them to full size; only three show in the collapsed fan and the rest wait until older ones dismiss.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add toast` writes `components/ui/toast/`. Import from `@/components/ui/toast`:

- Components and helpers: `Toaster`, `toastVariants`, `toast`, `useToast`, `useToastStore`, `TOAST_DURATION`, `ANCHORED_TOAST_DURATION`
- Types: `ToasterProps`, `ToastData`, `ToastOptions`, `ToastVariant`, `ToastAnchorRect`, `ToastPromiseMessages`, `ToastPromiseResult`
- Koala components it installs with it: `animated-label`, `button`, `spinner`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `hit-area`, `motion`, `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`, `radix-ui`
